chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'He decreed a term, and there is a term named with Him'
He said: 'These are two terms — a determined term and a suspended term.'

key_terms.أَجَلٌ مَحْتُومٌ: A determined/sealed term — the aspect of divine decree that is absolutely fixed and unchangeable
key_terms.أَجَلٌ مَوْقُوفٌ: A suspended/conditional term — the aspect of divine decree subject to bada', alterable by God based on circumstances
key_terms.الْبَدَاءُ: Bada' — the Shia theological doctrine that God can manifest a change in what appears to be His decree, without implying ignorance

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the determined term and the suspended term in Islamic theology?
ai.summary: Humran ibn A'yan asks Imam al-Baqir (AS) about the Quranic verse 6:2, which mentions two kinds of appointed terms. The Imam explains that one term (ajal mahmum) is definitively sealed by God's eternal decree, while the other (ajal mawquf) is conditional and subject to God's bada' — the divine capacity to alter outcomes based on changing circumstances or human actions. This hadith is foundational to Shia theology of bada', which affirms that while God's ultimate knowledge is complete, He may manifest different outcomes in time, preserving divine freedom and the efficacy of supplication and righteous action.

en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurara from humran from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.
“I asked the Imam about the words of Allah, “It is He who has created you from clay to live for a life-time and the span of your life is only known to Him. . .” [6:2]
The Imam said, “There are two appointed times. One is is a definit time and the other is the conditional one.”
